grade.rationale: The client is compact and generally readable, and deterministic evidence reports a successful .NET build. However, it accepts unsupported URI schemes, embeds potentially untrusted finding content directly into an agent prompt, masks a null projects response as a valid empty registry, and has limited cancellation and HTTP-error diagnostics. Test coverage is unknown.

summary: The implementation has a clear API and sensible DTOs, but its boundary validation and downstream-agent safety need strengthening. The most important issue is that review-derived text is interpolated directly into executable task instructions without a trust boundary. Configuration validation also accepts absolute non-HTTP URIs that HttpClient cannot send. Smaller issues concern silent handling of invalid project responses, discarded error bodies, and cancellation behavior during dry runs.

grade.rationale: Normal HTTP success paths are straightforward, but configuration regarded as valid can still fail because any absolute URI scheme is accepted, and a JSON null project response is incorrectly represented as an empty project list.

The records, method boundaries, naming, and centralized serialization settings are clear. More explicit configuration validation and shared endpoint construction would make failure behavior easier to understand and maintain.

The implementation is concise and documentation communicates its purpose well. Some behavior is misleading: IsTargetConfigured does not establish that the target is usable by HttpClient, and a null registry payload appears indistinguishable from a legitimate empty registry.

Failures are surfaced rather than silently swallowed in most paths, but non-success response details are discarded, invalid successful project payloads can be hidden, and dry-run output does not honor cancellation.

HttpClient and TextWriter injection plus the pure BuildCard method support focused unit tests. Mutable options and reliance on EnsureSuccessStatusCode make some boundary behaviors less explicit. No coverage data was supplied, so coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Configuration validation accepts URI schemes unsupported by HttpClient
findings.description: IsTargetConfigured and GetProjectsAsync only require an absolute URI. Values such as file:// or ftp:// therefore pass validation, after which HttpClient fails at send time because its request URI must use HTTP or HTTPS. This turns an invalid configuration into a misleading runtime transport failure.
findings.recommendation: Parse BaseUrl once and require its scheme to be Uri.UriSchemeHttp or Uri.UriSchemeHttps. Reuse that validated URI for endpoint construction and emit a configuration-specific exception for unsupported schemes.

findings.title: Review-derived content is inserted directly into downstream agent instructions
findings.description: FindingText and other review-controlled fields are interpolated into the task prompt alongside trusted instructions. A finding containing instruction-like text can alter the meaning of the generated task, add conflicting acceptance criteria, or induce the downstream agent to act on content copied from an untrusted reviewed file.
findings.recommendation: Treat every finding field as untrusted data. Prefer a task API that separates trusted instructions from structured finding data; otherwise clearly delimit and encode the fields, explicitly instruct the receiving agent that delimited content is evidence rather than instructions, and apply length and character limits before submission.

findings.title: A null projects payload is silently treated as an empty registry
findings.description: If the server returns a successful response whose JSON value is null, the method returns an empty list. That hides an invalid or incompatible server response and can make repository discovery appear legitimately empty.
findings.recommendation: Require a non-null list and throw an HttpRequestException or protocol-specific exception when the successful response does not contain the expected collection.

findings.title: HTTP failure responses lose useful server diagnostics
findings.description: EnsureSuccessStatusCode throws based on status alone, without reading any Agent Studio error payload. Callers consequently receive little context for configuration errors, validation failures, or server-side rejection of a card.
findings.recommendation: On non-success responses, read a bounded response body and throw an exception containing the endpoint, status code, and sanitized server message. Centralize this behavior so both endpoints report failures consistently.

findings.title: Dry-run output does not honor the operation's cancellation token
findings.description: The network path passes cancellationToken through, but the dry-run path uses the string WriteLineAsync overload without cancellation support. A canceled operation can therefore still write the full payload and return success.
findings.recommendation: Build the output string and use WriteLineAsync(output.AsMemory(), cancellationToken), or explicitly call ThrowIfCancellationRequested before and after writing if the target framework lacks the cancellable overload.
